title: FaxRxTx estimate
headline: FaxRxTx — the estimate, end to end
subject: Case FaxRxTx · worldwide fax send/receive back-end, second version (Venali, 2007–2009) · a participant's recollection · outcome known, opened after the estimate
standfirst: A fresh end-to-end estimate on the current chain: a product model, a work model and size classes by three isolated sensors, priced from a pinned table of external norms; an outside view by two independent launches; gap-blind Step C rates; a diagnosis that reconciled the units before attributing anything. The answer is 17 350 net task hours (about 152 staffed person-months), a rate corridor of 11 795–26 330, and an unresolved class tail. The remembered outcome, opened only after the document was fixed, is 120 staffed person-months — the centre is ×1.26 above it, inside the corridor.

Each outside curve was converted from its own declared unit (RC65-1: recorded 168-h months ×126 net h; RC65-2: staffed months ×114.5). The black mark is the outcome as remembered, ±20%. The fifty thin ochre curves are the no-method control of 17 September: five panels of ten bare agents on the same requirements and assumption log. The thick curves are the five panels after their Delphi: teal for the three that talked freely, ochre for the two that talked under three rules (a line includes its testing, a line cites the text, additions are put to a vote). Each thick curve is tall and narrow — a panel agrees with itself — and the five stand apart from one another by more than any of them admits: agreement inside a panel, disagreement between panels, none near the outcome. sections.title: How to read the chart
sections.lead: Both instruments produce a distribution. Only one of them did so without being asked.
sections.html:
Both instruments produce a distribution. The outside view produces quantiles natively; the bottom-up's range comes from the optimistic, most-likely and pessimistic value in every rate cell, summed under a declared item correlation of ρ = 0.5 — independent items would claim the total is known to about ±2%, perfectly correlated ones would give about ×1.9, and the truth is certainly neither. Across ρ from 0.25 to 0.75 the band edges move about ±20%. The width of the red bell is therefore a property of the rate table and of that convention, not of the project; what each curve's width does and does not contain is tabulated in docs/sensors/README.md.

Curves that must not be read as one

Each curve answers a different question. The outside view says where projects of this class landed against their early estimates — that width is the class's heterogeneity, the risk of the project. The bottom-up says what this work costs at the pinned rates — its width is the rates' spread under the declared correlation. A no-method family says what a bare model guesses on the same text, one thin curve per run, never pooled — its spread is the model's, not the project's. A parametric curve prices the functional shell only. Two readings of the outside view are one sensor run twice on the same input; where they disagree, the distance between them is that sensor's own uncertainty about the level, and neither is averaged with the other. Only the marked quantiles are readings; the curve between them is interpolation.

The unit, and the one conversion applied

Net hours of work on the task, shown as person-days of 8 such hours. Leave, public holidays and sickness are not in these numbers, and neither is any notion of calendar or headcount. Every sensor declares its own unit before its figures; the class readings are converted to task hours by the factor their own declarations contain, applied to the class side only — the bottom-up needs none, having been priced in task hours to begin with. The comparison-layer conversion to staffed person-months is the author's constant (docs/constants.md §4a) and appears in the text, never on the chart.

Known direction of error

The bottom-up curve is a normal approximation. Rate cells are right-skewed and correlated sums keep skew, so the true upper tail is fatter than drawn.

sections.title: Why the methods disagree
sections.lead: Units first, then blind spots; the two outside launches disagree with each other more than the chain disagrees with one of them.
sections.html:
units
Units component sized before anything was attributed 31% / 68% of the unit-blind gap
Read unit-blind (each outside month as 168 h), the outside view sits ×2.5 and ×1.8 above the chain. Converted by the pinned convention, the gaps are ×1.89 (RC65-1) and ×1.20 (RC65-2). The factor itself is disputed: 100–146 net h per RC65-1 month, 101–133 per RC65-2 month.
G1
A calibration factor that was a unit double count caught
Step C's G1 (within-day overhead ×1.25) turns net task hours into attended hours — the same step as the pinned 6-net-hours-a-day conversion. The chain is taken to G2 in net hours; the conversion to months replaces G1. Converting the post-G1 figure again would read ×1.58 against the outcome.
scope
Refused rows and holes +3 509 h
Immersion (W-F48) and the parallel-run comparison (W-F50) were refused as rows for undeclared headcount and period; Step C priced them as COCOMO II phase shares (T3 +999, T4 +874). Holes and closure findings, account load and performance testing priced through the table (+1 012); PM residual T5 +624.
systemic
Era, learning curve, complexity, growth +3 819 h
G2 era tooling and domain learning curve ×1.15 (+2 263, the largest and lowest-confidence item); T2 unnamed requirement growth ×1.12 (+1 294); T1 complexity of the hand-built orchestration and cluster ×1.17 (+262).
residual
Explained share, per reading 83% / overshoot
Against RC65-1: 83% explained, residual +1 552 h whose sign flips across the unit band. Against RC65-2: the corrections overshoot — the calibrated centre is ×1.44 above its P50 at every factor. Not closed by adjustment.

What Step C adds, and why the rates came out as they did

  • No generic uplift for testing, integration or rework — the coverage report showed the chain carries them heavily.
  • Omissions itemised (A1–A4) instead of a blanket percentage, which kept T2 at ×1.12 rather than ~×1.25.
  • A5 (cluster build-out) unpriceable — the table has no XL row for environments or hosting.
  • Two globals exactly: G1 (later ruled a unit) and G2.

False convergence, checked

The calibrated centre lands ×0.92 of RC65-1 — weak evidence: RK66's phase and complexity factors and RC65-1's anchor A-3 both come from COCOMO II, the agreement sits inside the unit band, and it is disagreement with RC65-2. The raw chain's ×1.20 closeness to RC65-2 was a coincidence of an incomplete chain and a low-anchored reading.

Above the outcome's own band by ×1.05. Without G2 the centre would read ×1.10; without T3–T5 ×1.05 — observations about where the miss sits, not corrections.

Rate corridor 11 795–26 330 h contains
The outcome sits 13% of the way up the envelope. The raw chain's ρ = 0.5 band (7 764–12 337) does not contain it; the raw chain was ×1.37 low.

Outside view brackets it ≈P30 / ≈P58
RC65-1 P50 ×1.38 high, RC65-2 P50 ×0.87 low; the outcome sits near RC65-1's P30 and RC65-2's P58.

End-to-end repeatability not measured (one product model priced); no human scale; one outcome in hand. Provenance held for the rates; the presence convention post-dates the outcome.

sections.title: Findings
sections.lead: Produced without being asked for, by instruments whose job was something else.
sections.html:
F-1
A pinned projection contaminated its consumer both repeats refused
assumptions_product.md quotes the immersion stage's duration in the paragraph that says it was removed. Both product-model sensors stopped at §1. The pinned file needs a new version.
F-2
The crossing cannot see obligation texts A9 refused
It refused performance testing on a statement whose obligation (F36) states a measurable target, because its input carries coverage ids only. Performance testing entered through Step C.
F-3
Two parser gaps in tools/chain silent drops
The consolidator misses group definitions written as '**NAME** is …' (49 items); the assembler misses special counts written as 'so the class is **M**'. Both handled by read-time wrappers; the tools were not changed.
F-4
Step C's G1 is a unit step request to the rate role
A global 'net hours → working hours' factor overlaps the pinned presence conversion; the diagnosis asked for it to be restated as a unit step.
F-5
Demanded rows need an output-bounded form catalogue
W-F48 and W-F50 cannot be priced as worded (headcount × period). The rate author proposed per-candidate evaluation, per-decision records, a comparator build, per-discrepancy-class adjudication and per-week monitoring.
F-6
F47 as a leaf is unsizeable both repeats
'First-version core function set, as replaced' declares a set it never names; the sizing sensors asked for an inventory of the first version's core functions.

sections.title: Defaults
sections.lead: Each is a fork the document leaves open and the estimate had to close. The reading taken is inside the centre; the reading refused is not. One row per entry of the assumption log, its first paragraph.
sections.html:
A1
Estimation scope
The full cycle for the "the team did" list from SYSTEM.md §6: the phase of domain immersion and architecture/technology selection (~1–2 months) + design + development + testing + rollout to production of the new version of the core functionality replacing the first version. - Included: rendering and OCR workers, the cluster with the delivery-control mechanism (watchdogs + tokens), NOC, the user portal, the inbound-email parser, saving CDR/billing data, integration tests on the real stream with comparison to the old system. - Not included: the PoP software, the routing program, billing,…
A2
Definition of Done
The new system takes production traffic in prod; the integration tests on the real stream have passed, the results agree with the old system; the old version can be decommissioned.
A3
Team and starting conditions
The team did not know the domain — immersion in the subject area, discussions, and technology selection took ~1–2 months (included in A1). Mitigating factor: a working v1 exists as a live reference of requirements ("like v1, but fix what we don't like") — there is no full-scale requirements gathering from scratch, but the domain (fax protocols, telecom, distributed delivery) is new to the team. Blended composition, including QA and PM. The team's headcount is not part of the assumptions (the volume of work is estimated, not the calendar).
A4
Reuse
No first-version code in the new one ("no reference base classes"). Reused: the ready PoP software, the ready routing, a third-party OCR library, rendering via a printer driver (Black Ice-class), the existing storage infrastructure (Lustre) and the DB as technologies — we do not develop these, only integrate with them.
A5
Technological era
2007–2009: C#/.NET ~3.x, a Windows cluster on our own hardware, no clouds and no ready orchestrators (what a message broker/Kubernetes would give today is written by hand — watchdogs, tokens, delivery control). MSMQ deliberately excluded from the negative experience of v1.
A6
Target scale
The engineering target — ~1 million faxes / 10-hour day (~30/s on average), with bursts up to ~10× (~300/s, "10 million/day" — an estimate of the peak mode). A cluster of ~16–20 nodes, 10–20 PoPs. The estimate is made for designing to the nominal with burst resilience: distribution, surviving failures, and delivery control of every fax are mandatory properties, not options.
A7
Rendering formats
8–10 input formats (DOC, XLS, PPT, PDF, TXT, GIF, TIFF + possibly 1–3 forgotten ones). Each format is a separate piece of integration and stabilization work, not a "free" extension of the list.
A8
Organizational context
A product company (Venali), an internal rework by management decision. There is no hard deadline, but there is pressure. The process — a planning phase, then scrum. Approvals are internal, faster than the enterprise client of the BMS example. Accounted for in reference class (decomposition, by construction, does not see it).
A9
Units
Estimation in person-months (1 pm ≈ 21 pd ≈ 168 hours), the total effort of the whole team, including QA/PM and the architecture-selection phase. Conversion to a calendar duration is a separate step, not part of the runs.

sections.title: Estimate gaps
sections.lead: Not oversights. Each is a thing the chain refused to price, with the reason it refused.
sections.html:
1
W-F48 and W-F50 as rows; cluster build-out (A5) awaiting a parameter
Headcount and length of the immersion and parallel-run stages undeclared; no XL row for environments and hosting. W-F48/W-F50 enter only as Step C shares.
2
The second product model ×1.10 unpriced
HM61-2 (75 leaves) was not crossed or sized; the end-to-end repeat is unmeasured.
3
The table's level and its day convention units question
External norms, uncalibrated; if its day-based sources meant assigned days, the chain is overstated ×1.23–1.45.
4
Migration, v1 upkeep, hyper-care, security, team grade no rate
Outside the declaration or uncovered by any rate; the reverse audit that would check the additive design has never been run.
5
Tail events and calendar class tail only
Orchestration collapse, driver/OCR instability, a failed parallel run: in the class quantiles only. Effort-to-calendar not estimated.

sections.title: Where every number came from
sections.lead: Each sensor is an engine with a version, stamped on its own output. They are hired for what they are forbidden to see, not for autonomy.
sections.html:
1
Product model · n = 2 · Hotyn-M 2.1 · run 61
47 product obligations → HM61-1: 84 elements, 68 leaves, 47/47 whole (closed); HM61-2: 91 / 75, F19 residue. Leaves ×1.10, coverage-set Jaccard 0.51. The first launch of both repeats stopped for contamination: the pinned product projection quotes a duration it says it removed; the figure was struck in the prompt and fresh instances launched.
2
Work model · Hotyn-W 1.2 · run 62
4 batches, one crossing each → 521 element-attached items, 0 row mismatches (after a read-time fix of one group-definition phrasing). F51 absorbed by the production cutover; F48, F49, F50, F52 standing as own branches.
3
Size classes · n = 2 · Hotyn-D 2.0 · run 63
64 / 63 leaves sized, 95.6% class agreement; 4 / 5 unsizeable (L27, L38, L51, L56; + L46). Assembly 10 094 / 9 747 net task hours, ×1.036.
4
Demanded-work rows · Hotyn-K 1.1 · run 64
W-F49 (62.7 h) and W-F52 (37.3 h) priced; W-F48 and W-F50 refused — headcount and parallel-run period undeclared. Raw chain 9 846–10 194 h.
5
Outside view · n = 2 · Lytin-R 1.1 · run 65
One class (in-house second-generation rewrite of a distributed back-end with a parallel-run cutover), 55% confidence. RC65-1 in recorded 168-h months, leave out: 80 / 150 / 240 / 310. RC65-2 in staffed months, leave in: 55 / 105 / 175 / 240.
6
Step C rates · Lytin-K 1.1 · run 66
Gap-blind. Fills A1–A5 (A5 unpriceable), T1–T5, two globals G1 (within-day overhead) and G2 (era + learning curve). Fills priced by the orchestrator's script through rate table v0.1-h.
7
Steps B, D · Lytin-G 1.1 · run 67
Units first: G1 duplicates the pinned 6-h day, chain stopped at G2. Centre 17 350 h, corridor 11 795–26 330, reserve = raw class tails. Explained 83% against RC65-1; overshoot against RC65-2.
0
No method ×50 in five panels, each run as a Delphi · runs 69–73, beside the estimate
Five panels of ten bare agents on the pinned prompt of run 41, all on 17 September. Thin ochre curves: the fifty independent round-1 answers. Thick teal: the consensus of the three free panels (A solid, B dashed, C dotted) — 126.5, 135, 147.5 pm. Thick ochre: the consensus of the two panels run under three rules — a line includes its testing, a line cites the text, additions are contestable by vote (D solid, E dashed) — 148 and 134 pm. The rules removed every invented line and every separate QA line and made removals as common as additions; they did not bring the panels together (×1.10 apart) and did not lower the level. The actual is 81.8 pm. Records: run69_delphi.md, run70_71_delphi_repeats.md, run72_73_delphi_rules.md. Not part of the run-61 estimate.

Two coordinates, not one

An estimate is a property of the triple (project × engine × model). Every sensor on this estimate ran on Claude Opus 5 (alias opus, recorded per turn as claude-opus-5), so the model coordinate is held fixed. Claude Code 2.1.270; every prompt reached its sensor byte-identical; every turn ended end_turn.

sections.title: Methodology
sections.lead: This report is one output of a method that is written down. Nothing below is specific to this case; every file states what it is for, what it may not do, and what would change it.
sections.html:
frame
METHODOLOGY.md
Why independence of techniques replaces independence of experts, what each method is structurally blind to, and why a divergence is diagnosed rather than averaged.
chain
docs/instrument.md
What actually runs: the product model, the crossing against a declared technology, the size classes, the pinned table, the script. What is pinned at each step and what each sensor is forbidden to produce.
curves

One note per curve on this chart: what the sensor was conceived as, what question it answers, what its width includes and leaves out, what has been measured about it, how to read its output, what may change.
numbers
docs/constants.md
Every constant the method has, and the comparison-layer conversion pinned by the author: 6 net task hours per present day, ×1.10 leave, 21 days — so 1 staffed person-month ≈ 114.5 net task hours.
case
docs/case_profile.md
Team grade, site count, domain familiarity and the outcome's unit are pinned before any estimate exists, so that no condition can be chosen after a number is on the table.
isolation
PIPELINE.md
The visibility matrix: who may see what, in what order the sensors are launched, and the disciplines that are mechanically checkable rather than promised.
prices
docs/rate_table.md · technology_catalogue.md
The pinned rates, in net person-hours, written gap-blind by a role that never saw a project total. And the vocabulary a technology declaration is written in.

When the instrument may be called fit for use, decided in advance: repeatability, position against human estimators, calibratability against outcomes.
this case
this case's folder
The pinned inputs, the case profile, the assumption log, the technology declaration, and every run with its raw sensor output kept verbatim.

fine: What this report is not. Not a validated price, and not a price at all — it is work content in net task hours, shown as person-days of 8 such hours. Converting it into money, calendar or headcount is the reader's act, using the reader's own figures. Every bottom-up number rests on a rate table of external industry norms calibrated against no outcome.

What it is. The estimate, its corridor, the disagreement between two structurally independent methods stated rather than averaged away, and, on the record, the obligations, the findings, the questions and the defaults that the number is standing on.
